findings.issue: أليس… كذلك؟ is the Arabic tag question 'isn't that so?', which asks the hearer to confirm that it IS so; the English floats the opposite proposition, 'it is NOT'. One hamza separates them: ليس كذلك؟ vs أليس كذلك؟. This holds on the string alone. Supporting context, not sequence: the only other fault line in this namespace is 'It's my fault, Uncle.' (DCD9C0794BDC866161CB4D9DD6FC5323), which is what the negative is about.

'Old man' here is dismissive — a peasant brushing off the goat-thief accusation in a scene that ends in a brawl. أيها الشيخ is deferential (elder/sheikh) and reverses the social direction of the insult. Also missing the comma before the vocative that the rest of the corpus uses.
